title: Connectivity Training
subtitle: Training relationships between signals rather than one amplitude
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating connectivity training within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain connectivity training without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in connectivity training.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to connectivity training.

sections.explainSimply: Connectivity training targets how activity at different sites covaries.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Measures can reflect genuine interaction, shared sources, reference effects or volume conduction. Different connectivity metrics are not interchangeable.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: A training target requires a clear metric, preprocessing pipeline and rationale. Apparent “normalisation” may reflect signal-processing choices.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Choosing a camera lens: every method emphasises some information and introduces its own distortions.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand connectivity training to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Shared artifact can create impressive but meaningless connectivity.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using connectivity training predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Shared artifact can create impressive but meaningless connectivity. Evidence classification: theoretical and emerging.
